summary: A 1961 R-6 flat-top ground cabin on Jumpoff Ridge in Yakima County, WA, replacing an earlier cupola cabin; volunteers stabilized it from 2010 and it is open to hikers.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Wenatchee National Forest

staffing.status: used sporadically on an emergency basis since the 1960s

access.note: Reached by a roughly 10-mile round-trip hike from Lost Lake; high-clearance vehicles can drive up. No closure found in these sources.

visit.trail_note: Trail from the Lost Lake trailhead, 10.0 miles round trip; the trail changes character several times on the way (WTA).

events.note: Newspaper item of October 18, 1921 reports a new lookout house completed on Jump Off; not clearly the same building
First structure, a D-6 cupola cabin (NHLR and Willhite)
Current R-6 cab replaced the cupola cabin between 1958 and 1961 (NHLR); Willhite says 1958 or 1961; Hiler says the earlier structure ran from the 1930s to 1958
Current R-6 flat-top cab; NHLR gives Built 1961, Hiler gives 1961
Mike Hiler was the lookout 1969 to 1973
Vandalism and neglect had broken windows, removed shutters and stripped lightning protection; Hiler and Friends of Jumpoff began stabilizing that summer, patching the roof and installing shutters
Stabilization by Mike Hiler and crew reported successful in the 2013 Eastern Washington chapter report
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register February 8, 2022; nominated by Mike Hiler

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The current cab is dated 1961 by the Register and by Hiler, and 1958 or 1961 by Willhite. The first structure is dated about 1923 by the Register and Willhite, while a 1921 newspaper item and Hiler's 1930s date point to other years. The story dates the current cab 1961 and reports the earlier dates as disputed.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: first-structure date (about 1923 per Register and Willhite; 1921 newspaper item; Hiler's 1930s to 1958 for the earlier cabin). Elevation differs: Register 5,749 ft, Willhite lookout 5,670 ft. The 2010 'before winter' detail in the brief was not found in the pages read; the story uses Willhite's and Hiler's wording. Access is from WTA and Willhite; no current Forest Service closure notice was checked. Staffing text is undated.
